If the Hooked Latch is distant from the chamber, it signifies estrangement.
Now that brothers are close to each other,
therefore the heavens draw near to illuminate this.
(Meaning "to reach" or "to attain")
Cānshīxīng (the Old Man Star)
The Records of the Grand Historian states:
In the northern region of Wolf, there is a great star called the Old Man of the South Pole.
When the Old Man appears, peace reigns;
when he is not seen, wars arise.
He is often observed during the autumn equinox in the southern suburbs.
The Book of Sui records:
The Old Man is a star located south of the Bow.
Another account says:
The South Pole is often seen at dawn during the autumn equinox,
and at dusk during the spring equinox,
some texts say at night,
it sets,
some texts say appears,
in the direction of Dīng. When seen, it signifies transformation and peace, and the ruler's longevity prospers.
The Monthly Ordinances state that on the day of the autumn equinox,
offerings are made to the Star of Longevity in the southern suburbs.
A commentary notes:
The Star of Longevity
is the Old Man of the South Pole star.
The Erya explains:
The Star of Longevity
refers to Jiǎo and Kàng.
A commentary adds:
The sequence begins with Jiǎo and Kàng,
the leaders among the constellations,
hence they are called
the Star of Longevity.
The Institutional History of Tang records:
During the Kāiyuán era, an edict ordered officials to establish an altar for the Star of Longevity on the Qiānqiū Festival day,
to perform sacrifices to the Old Man star and the seven stars of Kàng and Jiǎo,
making it a regular practice.
Jǐngxīng
The Records of the Grand Historian states:
When the sky is clear, the propitious star appears.
The appearance of the propitious star
signifies a star of virtue.
Its form is not constant.
It often appears in states governed by the Way.
The Illustrations of Auspicious Responses says:
The propitious star
is a large star.
Its shape resembles a half-moon.
It appears during the dark of the moon,
assisting the moon in providing light.
It appears when the ruler shows no favoritism.
Yuán Shānsōng's writings record:
During the reign of Emperor Huán of Hàn,
Chén Fān and Liú Zhīmào submitted a memorial stating:
"When the vital energy is vast, the propitious star appears;
when transformation is intricate, the five planets unfold."
Xú Líng's Inscription Beneath the Stūpa of Bàodé Temple for Emperor Wǔ of Chén says:
It assists the moon to bring forth the auspiciousness of the propitious star,
while ethereal mists flow with the colors of celebratory clouds.
Ominous Star
Ominous stars are called bó stars, comets, and long stars,
also known as chānqiāng.
The Astronomical Records states:
Bó stars
are a type of comet.
When they point sideways, it is called a comet's tail.
When their energy radiates in all directions, it is called bóbó,
meaning it appears scattered.
Their calamity is more severe than that of comets.
The Erya says:
Comets are called chānqiāng.
Sīmǎ Xiàngrú's "Rhapsody on the Great Man":
Grasped chānqiāng to use as banners.
Cuī Zhuàn of the Later Hàn's "Rhapsody on Consolation":
Wielded chānqiāng to sweep like lightning,
cleansing the lands within the six directions.
Xiè Zhān's "Poem on Zhāng Zǐfáng":
At Hóngmén, the eclipse faded; at Gāixià, it fell.
The note on chānqiāng: metaphor for a feather.
Dù Dǔ of the Later Hàn's "Discussion on the Capital" states:
Gāozǔ brandished the comet's light to sweep away Xiàng's army.
The note: comets signify removing the old and establishing the new, hence called sweeping.
Guànsuǒxīng
The nine stars of Guànsuǒ are in Qīgōng,
ahead is the prison entrance for the lowly,
one star is the gate,
if it wishes to open,
then there will be pardon,
if all nine stars are bright,
jails under heaven are troubled,
if seven stars appear, a small pardon,
six or five stars, a great pardon,
if they move, axes and fetters are used,
if the center is empty, the era changes.
"Shíshì Xīngjīng, Jìnzhì"
Sūn Dí says:
If the Tiānshì stars are numerous, the year is abundant,
if the Guànsuǒ stars are few, jails have no prisoners,
if Yínghuò bears a resting hue,
punishments are set aside unused.
Meteor
Huáinánzǐ: When a meteor is red in color,
it is called the Earth Goose.
Where it falls,
military forces will rise.
When a meteor has a bluish-red glow,
it is called the Heavenly Goose,
which is the essence of military armor.
Tiānwén Yàojí states:
When a meteor enters the Pleiades,
noble individuals will be imprisoned.
Strange Star
Yuán Shānsōng's Records state:
A strange star travels by day,
named Yíngtóu,
its passage portends great executions.
Guest Star
There are three guest stars:
the first is called Lǎozǐ,
the second is called the State Star,
and the third is called the Wēn Star.
Lǎozǐ refers to Lǐ Ěr,
an ancient man of virtue who did not serve in government,
and who lived to an old age with longevity.
As for the State Star,
it is Guóhuáng,
though it is unknown from which state he came.
As for the Wēn Star,
Wēn is his surname,
an ancient man of integrity who did not serve in government.
These three individuals,
their essences all became stars designated as guest stars.
"Zhōngxīng Astronomical Records"
Xuānyuán
The seventeen stars of Xuānyuán are located north of the Qīxīng constellation,
embodying the Yellow Dragon and presiding as the deity of thunder and rain,
symbolizing the imperial harem.
When yin and yang interact,
thunder stirs into lightning,
harmonizes into rain,
rages into wind,
chaoses into fog,
condenses into frost,
disperses into dew,
gathers into clouds,
and rising vapor forms a rainbow.
A halo separates into a dorsal arc,
while a parhelion splits into embracing halos,
all twenty-four transformations governed by Xuānyuán.
"Shǐ Zhèngyì"
Jīnhǔ
"Lù Shìhéng's Poem":
The Great Chen conceals its brilliance, the Golden Tiger reveals its substance.
"Shí's Classic of Stars" states:
The constellation Mǎo,
is the western lodge of the White Tiger.
Tàibái,
is the essence of metal.
When Tàibái enters the Great Mǎo,
metal and tiger press upon each other,
presaging military turmoil.
The spirit of the five elements
The two qi of yīn and yáng,
nurture all beings;
the essence and images find their lodging
in the sun and moon.
The nature of all living things
manifests as the five elements;
the numinous aspect of the five elements
is represented by the five planets.
"History of the Sòng Calendar"
The Essence of the Five Elements
The five stars are
the essence of the five elements.
The Five Emperors govern fate and respond to Heaven's commands, serving as Heaven's regulators.
《Qián Lǐ Xún Zhuàn》
Heaven has Five Emperors, with the five stars acting as their envoys.
． 《Suí Tiānwén Zhì》
The Five Assistants of Heaven
The five stars are
the Five Assistants of Heaven,
serving as the warp and weft, appearing and hiding,
sometimes passing through their orbits,
with expansions and contractions following fixed measures.
"Records of the Grand Historian"
Wǔ Chén
All stars rise in the east and set in the west,
thus the five planets are the five celestial markers,
and the twelve lunar mansions also serve as twelve celestial markers.
Jupiter governs solemnity and brings timely rains,
Mars governs wisdom and brings timely warmth,
Venus governs order and brings timely sunshine.
Mercury governs strategy and brings timely cold,
Saturn governs sagacity and brings timely winds.
The fixed stars remain constant and unchanging,
while the moving stars have periods of invisibility and appearance,
their advance and retreat following the sun's cycle.
Alternating cycles of flourishing, prosperity, decline, and decay
The Xing Bei states:
The five stars:
as they alternate between flourishing, strong, resting, and decay phases,
their colors differ.
In the flourishing phase, they are radiant;
in the strong phase, they are solid within;
in the resting phase, they are luminous
but without pointed rays and motionless;
in the decay phase, they have little light.
Their colors follow the four seasons,
and their corresponding states are all appropriate.
The Bao Zhang Shi Commentary explains:
Misgovernment
When governance fails in spring, Jupiter expands and contracts;
when governance fails in summer,
Mars moves retrograde;
when governance fails in autumn,
Venus appears and disappears irregularly;
when governance fails in winter,
Mercury does not appear in its proper station.
"Wénzǐ"
The Five Stars Converge
When Zhōu was about to attack Yīn,
the five planets converged in Fáng.
When Qí Huán was about to become hegemon,
the five planets converged in Jī.
When Hàn Gāo entered Qín,
the five planets converged in Dōngjǐng.
The "History of Sòng" records
the five planets converging in Jì,
and subsequently Wèi possessed the empire.
According to Yú Huàn's "Diǎn Lüè",
when the five planets converged in Jīwěi,
Ān Lùshān rebelled in Yān.
The "History of Táng" records
when Sòng Zǔ founded the state,
the five planets converged in Kuí;
when Tàizōng ascended the throne,
the five planets were in Kuí.
"History of Sòng"
The four stars converge
When four stars converged in the constellation Liǔ and Zhāng,
Emperor Guāngwǔ revived the Hàn dynasty in Luòyáng.
According to the "History of Sòng",
when four stars converged in the constellations Wěi and Jī,
Cáo Cāo welcomed the emperor,
established the capital in Xǔ, and stabilized Yǎn and Yù. Later,
four stars converged again,
and Emperor Wén of Wèi received the abdication.
As recorded in the "Records of Anomalies",
when four stars converged in the constellations Niú and Nǚ,
Emperor Yuán revived the Jìn dynasty in the Yáng region.
According to the "History of Jìn",
when Emperor Wǔ of Sòng launched the northern expedition,
four stars converged in the constellation Kuí;
and during the western expedition against Qín,
four stars converged in the constellation Jǐng,
four stars converged in the constellation Shēn,
marking the beginning of Bóhǎi's hegemony;
when four stars converged in the constellation Wēi,
Emperor Wénxuǎn received the throne.
According to the "History of Wèi",
when four stars converged in the constellation Zhāng,
Emperor Tàizǔ of Zhōu replaced the Hàn dynasty.
As recorded in the "History of the Five Dynasties".
Shēn Shāng
Zǐ Chǎn said:
In ancient times, Gāoxīnshì had two sons,
the elder named È Bó,
the younger named Shí Chěn,
who could not get along with each other.
They daily sought weapons to attack one another,
so the later emperor, disapproving of this,
relocated È Bó to Shěnqiū.
He presided over Chén for the Shāng people,
hence Chén became the star of Shāng.
He relocated Shí Chěn to
Dàxià, where he presided over Shēn for the Táng people,
hence Shēn became the star of Jìn.
"Zuǒzhuàn, Zhāogōng First Year"
Bó
Bó was originally from the time of Huángdì,
a woman who practiced cultivation but did not die a natural death.
"Zhōngxīng Tiānwén Zhì"
The Auspicious Star appears
The Records of the Grand Historian states:
During the time of Huángdì,
a propitious star appeared,
shaped like a half-moon,
enabling work at night.
The Central Prognostication of the Book of Documents states:
In the seventieth year of Emperor Yáo's governance of the seven celestial bodies,
a propitious star emerged.
The Wings of the Spring and Autumn Annals: Aiding the Appointed Times states:
During Shùn's era,
a propitious star appeared in the constellation Fáng.
The Five Elders of Yáo
The Apocrypha of the Analects states:
Zhòngní said:
I heard that Yáo led Shùn and others to tour Shǒu Mountain and observe the river islets,
where five elders were roaming.
One elder said:
The River Chart will come to announce the emperor's destined time.
The second elder said:
The River Chart will come to announce the emperor's strategy.
The third elder said:
The River Chart will come to announce the emperor's writings.
The fourth elder said:
The River Chart will come to announce the emperor's diagrams.
The fifth elder said:
The River Chart will come to announce the emperor's tally.
The dragon-borne king's envelope, sealed with golden clay and jade cases containing the documents, all proclaimed:
Those who know me,
are the double-pupiled Yáo and the five elders,
whereupon they flew away as shooting stars entering the constellation Mǎo.
Records of Omissions states:
"During Yú's reign,
five elders roamed in the capital,
and after abdicating to Yǔ,
the five elders departed,
and none knew where they went."
Yáo Tiánxīng
"The Ode to the Great Elephant" states:
The reverently bright light spreads everywhere,
Zhènxīng counterflows into the water palace,
the great waves surge to the heavens,
its merit is lofty.
Dà Yǔ notes:
In ancient times, Yáo encountered a great flood,
Zhènxīng moved counterflow into the water palace.
Shùn Huángxīng
Yuánwèi Zhāng Yuān's "Ode to Observing Celestial Phenomena":
Praising the yellow star's lack of锋芒,
Clarifying Yú Shùn's non-contention. Annotation:
In the past, when Shùn was about to receive the throne from Yáo,
A star first appeared,
Round and without sharp points,
Indicating that Shùn would rule the world with the virtue of earth.
The star appeared without pointed angles,
Symbolizing that he received the throne through abdication rather than military contention.
"Original Biography"
Luó Mì's "Grand History" states:
In the seventeenth year of Shùn's reign,
Heaven manifested ominous signs,
The yellow star lacked锋芒,
And the emperor then died.
The annotation cites this as evidence,
And considers Wèi to be different from Sòng, how strange.
The Emperor's Stellar Essence
Yáo's essence star is in the south,
its color red.
Shùn's essence star of the Dipper is in the center,
its color yellow.
Yǔ's essence star of the Three Stars is in the west,
its color white.
Tāng's essence star of the Emptiness is in the north,
its color black.
King Wén's essence star of the Room is in the east,
its color blue.
"Annotations to the Response to Essence Divination"
Xī Zhòng entrusted his essence
The "Ode on Observing Celestial Phenomena" says:
Xī Zhòng entrusted his essence to Jīnyáng.
Annotation:
Xī Zhòng,
four stars in the sky,
north of the ford near the riverbank.
In ancient times, the maker of chariots and carriages died,
and his essence ascended to become stars north of the river,
saying:
Yáng is north of the river,
hence called Jīnyáng.
The stars appeared as the cauldron was cast.
Wáng Zǐnián's "Shíyí Jì" states:
Yǔ cast the nine tripods,
selecting female metal for the yin tripods,
and male metal for the yang tripods.
The Great White Star appeared,
remaining visible for nine days without setting.
The Year Star Moves Forward
In the first year of King Tāng's reign,
the Year Star moved forward,
conjoining with the sun at the lunar mansions Fáng and Xīn,
which correspond to the regions of Sòng and Bó.
In the year following King Wǔ of Zhōu's arrival at Fēng,
the Year Star moved forward,
conjoining with the sun at the lunar mansions Liǔ and Zhāng.
Liǔ and Zhāng correspond to the regions between the Yellow River and the Luò River.
"Tīng Shǐ"
Fù Yuè riding the tail
The Zhuangzi says:
The Way can be transmitted but cannot be received,
it can be attained but cannot be seen. Fù Yuè attained it and became Wǔ Dīng's minister,
overseeing the entire realm, riding the Eastern Cord, mounting the Winnowing Basket and Tail, and ranking among the constellations.
The "Ode on Observing Celestial Phenomena" says:
Fù Yuè ascends to heaven and rides the Tail.
Annotation:
The star Fù Yuè is located behind the Tail,
riding the Tail between the dragon's team.
◇The "Shí Shì" states:
Fù Yuè is also called Tàizhù.
Zhèng Qiáo's "Comprehensive Records" states:
It is called Fù Yuè because
in ancient times there were governesses,
and there were nurses;
those who explain say that the governess delighted in it.
Coincidentally, the Fù Yuè of the Shāng dynasty
shares the same pronunciation,
and various scholars, not examining its meaning in detail,
then said that Yuè rides the Winnowing Basket and Tail,
not realizing that the Winnowing Basket and Tail
primarily govern affairs of the rear palace,
hence the assistance of Fù Yuè is there.
Note:
In heaven, they are stars and constellations;
among humans, they are sages and worthies;
in principle, this is naturally so.
But to alter antiquity and force an interpretation,
then Zào Fǔ, Xī Zhòng, and Yù Liáng were also ancients;
what explanation would there be for them?
Welcoming the New Year
King Wén of Zhōu received the Mandate,
with the Year Star in the Firebird constellation;
King Wǔ attacked Zhòu in the thirteenth year,
with the Year Star in the Firebird constellation.
The Biography of Sū Lín in the Records of Wèi states:
When King Wǔ attacked Zhòu,
he faced east to welcome the Year Star,
reached Sì where there was water,
and arrived at Gòngtóu where it fell.
A comet emerged,
presenting its handle to the people of Yīn.
At the time of battle, ten suns were in chaos above,
wind and rain struck in the midst,
yet there were no rewards for braving hardship ahead,
nor punishments for retreating behind.
Before the naked blades were fully drawn,
he had already conquered the world.
. The Huáinánzǐ's Instructions on Military Strategy states:
When King Wǔ attacked Zhòu,
Yú Xīn admonished saying:
"The Year Star is in the north; do not march northward."
King Wǔ did not follow this advice.
From the Shīzǐ.
Tiānyuán
The Discourses of the States states:
Líng Zhōujiū replied to King Jǐng of Zhōu:
When King Wǔ attacked Yīn,
the year-star was in Chúnhuǒ,
and the constellation was in Tiānyuán.
Our Jī clan originated from Tiānyuán,
and Tiānyuán is Xuánxiāo,
which corresponds to the division of Qí.
The mother of Wáng Jì,
Tài Jiāng, was a woman of Qí,
hence it is said to originate from Tiānyuán.
Dreaming of the Big Dipper
The "Ode on Observing Celestial Signs" states:
When Lǚ Shàng dreamed at night,
He excelled in ascending to assist and support the sage.
The annotation says:
In the past, when Tàigōng had not yet encountered King Wén,
He was fishing at Pánxī and dreamed at night of the deity of the auxiliary star of the Big Dipper,
Who informed Shàng of the intention to attack Zhòu,
． This event is recorded in the chapter "Shàngshū Zhōnghòu."
After the sacrifice was completed,
The Net is the celestial net,
governing the entrapment of unprincipled rulers.
Thus, when King Wǔ of Zhōu attacked King Zhòu,
he offered sacrifices to the Net above,
seeking assistance from Heaven.
． "Biography of Sū Jìng in the Book of the Later Hàn"
Jiǔguāng
King said:
"I do not know the light of the nine stars."
Zhōu Gōng Dàn said:
"The nine stars,
are the stars, planets, sun, moon, four seasons, and year—these are called the nine stars,
the nine stars,
nine lights."
The "Zhōu Shū"
Rèn Fǎng's earnest exhortation to the King of Liáng stated:
"Reconstructing Shēn and Chén, and the nine stars look up to them,
not altering the sun and moon, and the two principles remain steadfast in their observation."
Gǎn Xīng
Wēizǐ was moved by the Altair star,
Yán Yuān was moved by the Middle Platform star,
Zhāng Liáng was moved by the Bow star,
Fán Kuài was moved by the Wolf star.
"The Master Liú"
A five-colored comet pierced through the Ziwei Enclosure.
In the final years of King Zhāo’s reign,
a comet appeared,
its light of five colors piercing through the Ziwei Enclosure.
The people of Jīng sent humble words to the king, saying:
"We wish to present a white pheasant."
They secretly had people by the Hàn River prepare a boat glued with resin to await the king.
The king then made a southern tour of inspection,
intending to reach the sea, but the sky grew dark and overcast, and pheasants and hares were all startled.
The six armies were lost at the Hàn River.
When the king reached midstream,
the resin dissolved and the boat fell apart.
The king, along with Duke Jìgōng and Xīn Yúmí, drowned.
From the "Bamboo Annals"
Zàofù and Wángliáng
The "Ode on Observing Celestial Phenomena" states:
Looking up, one sees Zàofǔ and also Wáng Liáng.
Annotation:
Zàofǔ,
five stars located in the Guest House within the River,
Zàofǔ, the charioteer of King Mù of Zhōu, his essence ascended to become a star upon his death.
Wáng Liáng, five stars situated north of Kuí,
Wáng Liáng was
a great officer of Jìn, skilled in charioteering, the son of Jiǔfāng.
◇ Liáng also known as Yóu Wúzhèng,
served as charioteer for Zhào Jiǎnzǐ.
Upon his death,
his essence lodged among the stars,
becoming the celestial emperor's charioteer official.
Hán Yáng's "Essential Collection of Astronomy" says:
Zàofǔ washes the horses,
with reins, bridles, and bits.
The "Records of the Grand Historian" states:
Wáng Liáng whips the horses,
chariots and cavalry fill the wilderness,
the Northern Dipper and the Three Platforms flow together.
During the time of King Lì of Zhōu,
the Northern Dipper and the Three Platforms flowed together,
their whereabouts unknown.
After King Lì's demise,
the two ruling stars reappeared.
"Records of Unique Anomalies"
Observing Stars to Recognize the Hegemon
The "Ode on Observing Celestial Signs" says:
Admiring Guǎn Zhòng's discernment of subtleties,
he saw the alignment in Xū and Wēi and thus knew the mandate.
The annotation states:
In the past, Guǎn Zhòng and Bào Shūyá were traveling merchants in Nányáng,
when they observed three stars gathering in the region of Xū and Wēi.
Knowing that Qí would produce a hegemon,
they then joined forces
and went to pledge their service in the land of Qí.
The stars are not visible.
On the day Xīnmǎo in the fourth month,
the fixed stars were not visible at night,
and at midnight stars fell like rain.
"Zuǒzhuàn, Duke Zhuāng, seventh year"
A comet entered the Dipper.
King Xiāng of Zhōu was unable to serve his mother and younger brother properly,
a comet entered the Dipper constellation,
and it lost its regular course.

Xuánxiāo
In spring there was no ice,
Zǐ Shèn said:
"This year Sòng and Zhèng will suffer famine.
The year-star is in Xīng Jǐ,
but has trespassed into Xuán Xiāo.
The snake rides the dragon,
and the dragon
is the star of Sòng and Zhèng.
Sòng and Zhèng must suffer famine.
Xuán Xiāo is empty at the center.
Xiāo
means 'exhaustion'.
When above is empty and the people are exhausted, how can they avoid famine?"
(Zuǒzhuàn, Xiānggōng 28th Year)
A comet appeared in the constellation Chén.
In winter, a comet appeared to the west of the Great Star and reached the Han River.
Shēn Xū said:
"The comet is used to sweep away the old
and establish the new.
Now it sweeps away the fire,
and when the fire appears, it will surely spread.
Will the feudal lords have fires?"
Zǐ Shèn said:
"It will be in Sòng, Wèi, Chén, and Zhèng."
Zhèng's Bì Zào said to Zǐ Chǎn:
"Sòng, Wèi, Chén, and Zhèng will have fires on the same day.
If we use the guàn guàn jade libation cup,
Zhèng will certainly not have a fire."
The people of Zhèng requested to use it.
Zǐ Chǎn said:
"The way of Heaven is distant,
the way of man is near.
They are not connected.
How can Zào know the way of Heaven?"
So he did not give it,
and there was also no fire.
"Zuǒzhuàn", the eighteenth year of Duke Zhāo.
Obtained the Year
Wú attacked Yuè,
Shǐ Mò said:
In less than forty years,
will Yuè possess Wú?
Yuè has obtained the Year Star's influence while Wú attacks it,
Wú is bound to suffer its misfortune.
"Zuǒzhuàn, Zhāogōng 32nd Year"
Warding Off the Comet
In Qí there was a comet,
Duke Jǐng sat in the Bǎi Qǐn hall and wept,
Yànzǐ asked him about it.
The Duke said:
I have heard that,
when a comet appears,
the ruler of the country it points toward will face its consequences.
Now the comet has appeared and is pointing toward our state,
therefore I grieve.
Yànzǐ said:
Your actions and righteousness,
surely have brought no virtue to the state,
digging ponds and pools you desire them deep and wide,
building towers and pavilions you want them high and large,
tax collection is like plunder,
executions are like dealing with enemies,
from Yìng's perspective,
another comet will appear again,
why fear the appearance of this comet?
The Duke wanted to send Cháng Bó Qiān to perform an exorcism against it,
Yànzǐ said:
It is useless,
only inviting deception,
the Way of Heaven is neither partial nor divided,
how can its mandate be altered?
Performing exorcisms,
if spirits could be prayed to come,
they could also be exorcised to leave.
The people's suffering and grievances number in the tens of thousands,
yet you order one person to perform exorcism,
how can that overcome the voices of the multitude?
"Records of the Grand Historian" "Yànzǐ's Spring and Autumn Annals" "Zuǒ Zhuàn"
Observing the Stars to Know the Earth's Movements
Duke Jǐng of Qí asked the Grand Diviner:
"What can your art accomplish?"
He replied:
"I can make the earth shake."
The Duke told Yànzǐ this,
and Yànzǐ went out to see the Grand Diviner, saying:
"Previously I saw the Hooked Star between Fáng and Xīn,
so was the earth about to shake?"
The Grand Diviner said:
"Yes."
Yànzǐ left,
and the Grand Diviner hastened
to see the Duke's minister.
"I cannot make the earth shake;
the earth was going to move of its own accord."
Lùnhéng
Yànzǐ saw Cháng Bóqiān
and asked him:

and the Pivot Stars scattered,
so was the earth about to shake?"
Yànzǐ Chūnqiū
A comet veils the moon.
The Later Chronicle of the Spring and Autumn Annals states:
The man of Wèi, Táng Jū, replied to the King of Qín:
When Zhuān Zhū assassinated King Liáo,
a comet swept across the sky,
and the moon lost its color.
The Purple Tenuity emits radiance.
When Zhòngní completed the Spring and Autumn Annals,
the Purple Tenuity emitted radiance.
From Bàopǔzǐ
A comet appeared in the east.
In the eleventh month of the thirteenth year of Duke Āi of Lǔ,
a comet appeared in the eastern sky.
The following year,
the events recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals came to an end.
This is said to mark the decline of the various Xià states,
the dominance of the barbarian tribes,
the Tián clan's monopolization of Qí,
the three families' usurpation of Jìn,
ultimately leading to their encroachment upon their rulers' authority and the gradual decline of rightful succession,
thus beginning the Warring States period,
when the world fell into chaos.
Book of Wèi
A comet appears in the northeast.
During the Spring and Autumn period,
when a comet appeared in the north,
the rulers of Qí, Lǔ, Jìn, Zhèng, Chén, Sòng, and Jǔ all suffered violent deaths and turmoil.
When a comet appeared in the east,
Chǔ destroyed Chén and the Three Families,
from which point they began to divide and seize power from Qí and Jìn.
The Book of Sòng records
that during the time of Duke Jǐng of Sòng, the planet Mars retreated from its lodge.
Mars remained in the Heart constellation.
The Heart constellation
corresponds to the domain of Sòng.
Duke Jǐng was troubled by this.
The astrologer Zǐ Wéi said:
"It can be transferred to the prime minister."
The Duke said:
"The prime minister
is my right-hand man."
Zǐ Wéi said:
"It can be transferred to the people."
The Duke said:
"A ruler depends on the people."
Zǐ Wéi said:
"It can be transferred to the harvest."
The Duke said:
"If the harvest fails and the people suffer,
for whom would I be ruler?"
Zǐ Wéi said:
"Heaven is high but hears what is below,
you have spoken three words worthy of a true ruler,
Mars should move accordingly."
They waited and observed,
and indeed it shifted three degrees.
The Annals of Lǚ Bùwéi
How does the comet know?
In the past, General Zǐzhèng of Chǔ was about to engage in battle with Qí.
Before the armies clashed at night,
a comet appeared,
with its tail pointing toward Qí.
According to the belief, the side it pointed to would be victorious,
making it inadvisable to attack.
Zǐzhèng said:
"What does a comet know?"
The next day, he fought the Qí army and utterly defeated them.
From "Wèi Liáo Zǐ":
When Venus eclipsed the Pleiades,
as mentioned in a letter from Zōu Yáng of the Former Hàn Dynasty to King Xiào of Liáng:
Mr. Wèi devised the strategy for Qín in the Chángpíng campaign.
Venus eclipsed the Pleiades,
causing King Zhāo to doubt him.
Sū Lín explained:
Bái Qǐ, leading Qín's forces against Zhào, defeated the army at Chángpíng.
Intending to annihilate Zhào completely,
he sent Mr. Wèi to persuade King Zhāo to supply more troops and provisions.
However, Mr. Wèi was harmed by Yìnghóu,
and the plan failed.
His utmost sincerity reached up to Heaven,
thus causing Venus to eclipse the Pleiades on his behalf.
A comet appeared at Dàjiǎo.
The Qin historical records state:
During the reign of the First Emperor,
a comet appeared near Arcturus.
The Western Han anthology records:
When Xiàng Yǔ was defeated,
a comet appeared near Arcturus.
Liú Xiàng said:
When the three dynasties fell, the stars of the Great Bear changed their positions;
when Qín and Xiàng Yǔ perished,
a comet appeared near Arcturus.
The Five Stars Converge in the Southern Dipper
During the reign of the Second Emperor of Qín, the five planets converged in the Southern Dipper,
and the commandant of Nánhǎi, Rén Xiāo, said:
"Qín is about to enter a prolonged period of chaos,
this is an omen of partial hegemony for Nányuè,"
and thus he formed an ambition.
As he fell ill and was near death,
he summoned Zhàotuó from Zhēndìng to administer the affairs of the Nánhǎi commandant,
which is why he is now called Commandant Tuó.
Emperor Gāozǔ of Hàn sent Lù Jiǎ to establish him as the King of Nányuè.
"Records of Nányuè"
Tàibái Stole the Weaver Girl's Maidservant
When Qin annexed the six states,
the Star of Venus secretly took the Weaver Girl's attendant.
Liáng Yùqīng and Wèi Chéngzhuāng fled into the Small Immortal Cave in Yá City,
and did not emerge for forty-six days.
The Heavenly Emperor grew angry,
ordered the Five Sacred Mountains to search and capture them,
the Star of Venus returned to his post,
and Wèi Chéngzhuāng escaped.
Yùqīng had a son named Zǐxiū,
Yùqīng was banished below the Big Dipper to pound herbs eternally,
and her son was assigned to accompany the River Earl as an attendant in making rain.
Whenever Zǐxiū reached the Small Immortal Cave,
he was ashamed of the place where his mother had eloped,
and would always turn his carriage away without passing through,
so this place often had little rain.
"Dōngfāng Shuò's Inner Biography and Records of the Extraordinary"
The stray arrow flew westward.
The Book of Hàn states:
When Xiàng Yǔ came to the rescue of Jùlù,
a crooked arrow shot westward,
wherever the crooked arrow struck,
it became the target of the world’s punitive attacks,
a portent of destruction.
Thus, Xiàng Yǔ formed alliances,
buried the Qín people alive,
and massacred Xiányáng.
Whenever a crooked arrow appears,
it signifies chaos quelling chaos.
Zhāng Héng’s "Rhapsody on Celestial Phenomena of the Zhou Dynasty" says:
The serpent followed Chǔ, and the nine domains sighed in sorrow.
The "Rhapsody on Observing Celestial Phenomena" states:
The constant star remained unseen as Zhōu declined,
and the crooked serpent slithered as Qín perished.
Tiānjiē
The Records of the Grand Historian states:
During the siege of Píngchéng,
the moon was haloed sevenfold around the constellations Shēn and Bì.
The Book of Han says:
Between Bì and Mǎo,
lies the Celestial Street.
North of the Street are the Hú peoples,
south of the Street is Zhōngguó (the Central States).
Mǎo represents the Xiōngnú,
Shēn represents Zhào,
Bì represents the border troops.
That year,
Emperor Gāozǔ personally led his army to Píngchéng,
was besieged by Mòdú,
and the siege was lifted only after seven days.
The essence of the Pleiades star
The Spring and Autumn Annals and Its Supplements states:
The Han dynasty's chancellor, Xiāo Hé,
was seven chi and eight cun tall,
and was born from the essence of the Pleiades star.
He had three folds in his ears, a prominent forehead, and a hooked nose.
The Decree of Fate states:
Xiāo Hé was the essence of the Pleiades,
while Xiàng Yǔ, Chén Shèng, and Hú Hài were the three disruptors.
Tiāngǒu
In the eighth month of the second year of Emperor Wén of Hàn's later reign, a celestial dog descended;
in the seventh month of the third year of Emperor Jǐng's reign in Liángyě, a celestial dog descended;
the descent of the celestial dog served as a warning for defense.
That year,
Wú and Chǔ rebelled and attacked Liáng;
Liáng fortified its city and held its ground,
resulting in corpses lying and blood flowing beneath it.
"The Ode of the Great Elephant" states:
When the dog crosses Liáng, blood flows for a thousand miles.
A guest star obscured the imperial throne.
Emperor Wǔ once traveled incognito to a host's home,
where he stayed overnight.
At night, he slept with the host's maidservant,
while a scholar was also lodging there.
Skilled in astronomy, the scholar suddenly saw a guest star about to obscure the imperial throne, approaching very closely.
The scholar exclaimed in alarm,
unintentionally raising his voice.
He then saw a man carrying a knife about to enter the room,
but upon hearing the scholar's urgent cry,
he immediately retreated and fled.
The guest star then receded at that moment.
This happened several times,
and the emperor, finding it strange, inquired about it.
The scholar recounted everything he had witnessed,
upon which the emperor realized and said:
"This must be that person's son-in-law,
intending to commit violence against me."
He then instructed the host to summon the imperial guards to capture the servant,
who confessed upon interrogation and was executed.
The emperor sighed and said:
"This was surely Heaven enlightening the scholar to protect me,"
and thus generously rewarded the scholar.
Records of the Hidden and Visible Worlds
Zhé mù zhǐ huì
Emperor Wǔ once saw a comet,
and Fāng Shuò broke off a branch from a tree that pointed to the stars and handed it to him.
The emperor used it to point at the comet,
and the comet then vanished.
On the night the star appeared,
wild beasts all cried out,
some say it was the "Beast-Crying Star."
From Guō Zǐhéng's "Records of Penetrating the Obscure."
The Emperor's Supreme Majesty
Of the nine stars of the Dipper, seven are visible and two are hidden;
the eighth and ninth are the spirits of the supreme emperor and sovereign.
During the Han dynasty, Huò Guāng, the Chancellor of State, had a servant in charge of clothing named Huán Chē,
who suddenly saw two stars within the Dipper shining with extraordinary brightness.
He bowed in reverence and returned,
and thus gained an additional six hundred years of life.
"The Precious Sea Scripture of the Mysterious Gate"
The stars all tremble
During the Yuánguāng era, all the stars in the sky shook,
and the Emperor questioned the star observers about it.
They replied:
"When the stars shake,
it means the people are toiling."
Later, campaigns were launched against the Four Barbarians,
and the common people were wearied by warfare.
The "Inner Biography of the Hànshū" attributes this to Dōngfāng Shuò.
Suìjīng
The Queen Mother dispatched an envoy who arrived,
and Dōngfāng Shuò died.
The Emperor questioned the envoy, who replied:
"Shuò is the Wood Emperor,
whose essence is the Year Star,
who descended among humans to observe the world,
and is not Your Majesty's subject."
"Hanwu Neizhuan"
A comet appeared in the constellation of Qiānniú.
In the second year of Emperor Āi's Jiànpíng era,
a comet emerged in the constellation Qiānniú.
This constellation marks the starting point
for calendrical calculations and
the beginning of the three celestial standards.
For a comet to appear there
signified an omen of change,
which was later followed by Wáng Mǎng's usurpation of the throne.
Hànshū
The divine star appears by day
Emperor Guangwǔ was defeated.
Wáng Xún wrote to Zhū Rán, saying:
On the day of battle,
the planet Mars appeared in the daytime, and Venus was clear and bright.
From "Dōngguān Hànjì"
The three stars are in the division of Hàn.
During the time of Wáng Mǎng, bandits and rebels rose in groups.
Zhì Yùn looked up and observed the celestial phenomena,
sighing as he said to his friend:
"Now, Zhèn Suì and Yíng Huò are both present,
in the region of the division of Hàn, between Yì and Zhěn, having left and returned again.
Hàn is destined to receive the mandate; blessings will return.
If there is one with virtue who follows heaven's will to devise strategies,
they are certain to achieve great success."
From the "History of the Later Hàn,"
the Yǎn Kǒng Diagram states:
"The characters for '卯金刀' form the name Liú,
who departed from Jīngzhōu in the southeast of the Central State,
hence it became the division of Hàn."
Stars orbit
On the evening when Liú Shènggōng first obtained the imperial seal and ribbons,
a meteor descended like a rope coiling around Shènggōng.
The next day, he was strangled by Liú Pénzǐ's general Xiè Lù,
which also corresponded to the omen of the coiling star.
Hòu Hàn shū
Two envoys
When Emperor Hé ascended the throne,
he separately dispatched two envoys to each province and commandery to observe and collect folk ballads.
The two men were to arrive in Yì Province,
and sought lodging at the residence of Hòu Guǎn official Lǐ Hé.
Sitting outdoors on a summer night,
Lǐ Hé asked: When you two gentlemen departed from the capital,
did you know the court had dispatched two envoys to the commandery?
When asked how he knew this,
Lǐ Hé pointed to the stars and said:
There are two envoy stars coming toward Yì Province.
"Book of Hàn"
Mainland
The Biography of Lǔ Gōng in the Book of the Later Han states:
If the decrees of autumn are implemented in midsummer,
then people will be harmed by epidemics,
as the energy of the Great Mound becomes harmful.
The "Chūnqiū Héchéng Tú" states:
The star of the Great Mound governs death and mourning.
It is also called "Jīshī Juǎnshé."
Galloping, the stars stand still
Zhōu Téng,
styled Shūdá,
served as an Attendant Censor.
When Emperor Huán was to perform the southern suburban sacrifice,
he was scheduled to depart at dawn,
but Téng looked up and observed:
"The sovereign mirrors the stars,
yet now the Palace Star and the Chariot-Horse Stars remain motionless;
he surely will not depart tomorrow."
By the fourth watch,
the Crown Prince had died,
and the ceremony was halted.
"Biographies of Exemplary Persons from Yùzhāng"
A virtuous star appears
The Grand Historian said:
"A virtuous star has appeared,
indicating that there are talented and virtuous individuals traveling together."
An imperial edict was issued to all commanderies and counties,
inquiring specifically about Yǐngchāng Commandery.
The official report stated:
"There are three members of the Chén family—Chén Tàiqiū and his two sons—gathered together for a community feast."
The Miscellaneous Affairs of Hàn records:
"Chén Tàiqiū visited Xún Lǎnglíng,"
and so on,
and so forth,
at which time the Grand Historian reported that a true man was traveling east.
Shì Shuō.
Virtuous Stars Converge
Chén Zhònggōng took his sons and nephews to visit Xún Jìhé and his sons,
at that time virtuous stars gathered.
The Grand Astrologer reported that within five hundred li, wise men had assembled.
"Yì Yuàn"
records that the brothers visited Xún Shuàng at night.
"Rǔnán Xiánxián Zhuàn"
The Southern Dipper Registers Life
Guǎn Lù arrived at Píngyuán,
and seeing Zhào Yán's countenance foretold an early death,
Yán's father then begged Lǔ to prolong his life.
Lǔ said:
Return home,
find clear wine and a jin of dried venison,
on a Mǎo day, go to the large mulberry tree south of the wheat field you'll reap,
there will be two men playing weiqi, pay them no mind,
just pour the wine and set out the dried meat,
when they finish drinking, refill until it's all gone.
If they ask you,
only bow to them,
say nothing.
Surely someone will save you, Yán.
He went as instructed,
and indeed saw two men playing weiqi.
Yán set out the dried meat and poured wine before them,
the men, absorbed in their game, just drank and ate without looking up.
After several rounds of drinking,
the one sitting north suddenly noticed Yán there,
shouted:
Why are you here?
Yán only bowed.
The one sitting south said:
We've just consumed his wine and meat,
how can we be without feeling?
The north sitter said:
The document is already fixed.
The south sitter said:
Lend me the document to see.
Seeing Zhào's lifespan was set at nineteen years,
he took a brush and altered it above,
said to Yán:
I save you to live until ninety years.
Yán bowed and returned,
Guǎn told Yán:
Great help for you!
Rejoice in gaining increased longevity.
The north sitter was the Northern Dipper,
the south sitter was the Southern Dipper,
the Southern Dipper registers life,
the Northern Dipper registers death,
all humans upon conception pass from the Southern Dipper to the Northern Dipper,
all prayers and requests are directed to the Northern Dipper.
"Sōu Shén Jì"
The Eastern Dipper governs reckoning,
the Western Dipper records names,
the Northern Dipper decrees death,
the Southern Dipper elevates life,
the Central Dipper, the great chief,
oversees all spirits.
"Dù Rén Jīng"
The Chariot constellation pursues ghosts,
the Net constellation detains souls,
the Eastern Well returns the po.
"Bào Pú Zǐ"
The general's star falls
A star, red and radiant with pointed rays,
moved from the northeast to the southwest,
vanishing into Zhūgě Liàng's camp,
and shortly thereafter, Liàng passed away.
"Sūn Shì Jìnyáng Qiū"
Mars Transforms into a Child
In the first year of the Yǒng'ān era of Sūn Xiū of Wú,
there were various hostages playing among a group.
There was one extraordinary child whose eyes had a radiance,
shining and projecting outward.
The other children asked him:
"I am Mars,"
"I will show you that the Three Dukes will return to the Sīmǎ family."
After speaking, he raised his body and leaped,
looking up, it was as if dragging a bolt of white silk,
after a moment, he vanished.
Four years later, Shǔ perished,
six years later, Wèi was abolished,
twenty-one years later, Wú was pacified,
this was the return to Sīmǎ.
From the "Book of Sòng"
"In Search of the Supernatural":
The Three Dukes yield to Sīmǎ Xiàngrú.
The Central Terrace Splits Apart
Zhāng Huà served as Minister of Works,
when the central star of the Ursa Major constellation split,
his youngest son Zhāng Wěi urged him to resign from his position.
Zhāng Huà said:
"The ways of heaven are mysterious and distant,
one must cultivate virtue to respond to them."
Records of the Jin Dynasty
When Zhāng Huà was about to die,
the central star of the Ursa Major constellation broke,
during the Taiyuan era it returned to its original state,
which was attributed to Grand Tutor Xiè Ān becoming chancellor.
Annals of Jin Yang
The moon encroaches upon Shaowei
In Kuàijī, Xiè Fū, styled Qìngxù,
lived in seclusion on Mount Ruòyē.
At that time, the moon encroached upon the Shǎowēi star.
The Shǎowēi star is also called the Hermit Star,
and astrologers believed it corresponded to a hermit.
Dài Kuí of Qiáo was more renowned than Xiè Fū,
so people were concerned for him.
Soon after, Xiè Fū died.
Thus, the gentry of Kuàijī mocked the people of Wú, saying:
"The eminent scholar of Wúzhōng
is one who seeks death but cannot attain it."
From "Jìnyáng Qiū".
A baleful star appeared in the Yúzhōu region.
Initially, an ominous star appeared in the region corresponding to Yùzhōu.
Lìyáng's Chén Xùn once remarked to people:
"This year, a great general of the northwest shall die."
Zǔ Tì also observed the star and said:
"It is for me.
Just as I am about to pacify Héběi, Heaven wishes to kill me—
this shows it does not protect the state."
He soon died at Yōngqiū.
(Book of Jìn)
Drink the Shooting Star
Yuán Zhēn was in Yùzhōu,
and sent his female entertainers Jìlíng Ā Bì, Ā Guō, and Ā Mǎ to Huán Xuānwǔ.
After they had been there for some time,
the three went out together on a summer night.
Under the moonlight, there was a bronze jar with water beside it.
They saw a shooting star fall into the jar.
Surprised and delighted, they all looked at it.
The star was like a two-inch fiery pearl,
shining brightly and clearly at the bottom of the water.
They then said to each other:
"This is an auspicious sign,
but who will it correspond to?"
Thereupon, Bì and Guō took turns trying to scoop it up with a ladle,
but neither succeeded.
Mǎ was the last to try to scoop the star,
and it went right into the ladle.
She then drank it.
Soon after, she seemed to have a sensation,
and shortly became pregnant with Huán Xuán.
Although Huán Xuán's usurpation of the throne did not last,
for several years he enjoyed the pinnacle of glory and nobility.
(Continuation of In Search of the Supernatural and Continuation of the Autumn Annals of Jìnyáng)
A star fell and transformed into flesh.
The Hàn ruler Liú Cōng was excessively licentious and unrestrained.
At that time, a star fell in Píngyáng and turned into flesh.
It measured twenty-eight paces in diameter.
The ministers admonished him, attributing it to his debauchery.
Liú Cōng said:
This is a matter of the celestial family,
what does it have to do with me?
"Spring and Autumn of the Sixteen Kingdoms"
Liú Cōng said:
This is the principle of yīn and yáng,
how is it related to human affairs?
"Records of the States"
The planet Venus trespasses against the Eastern Well.
When Fú Shēng was alive,
someone reported that Venus had trespassed against the Eastern Well,
and the Well corresponds to the region of Qín.
The appearance of Venus portends punishment,
and there must be violent soldiers rising in the capital.
Shēng said:
As for the star entering the Well,
it was merely thirsty itself—
what is there to find strange about it?
"Records of the Carried Chronicles"
Fúdé was in Yān.
Fú Jiān attacked Yān,
and the people of Yān were greatly shaken.
Féng Fú asked Shēn Shēng:
"What will become of this situation?"
Shēng sighed and said:
"Yè is doomed to fall.
However, when Yuè gained the year's favor and Wú attacked it, Wú ultimately suffered disaster.
Now virtue and blessings reside with Yān.
Although Qín may achieve temporary success,
Yān's restoration will occur within no more than twelve years."
When Mùróng Wěi surrendered Yān,
the former Grand Astrologer Huáng Hóng sighed and said:
"Yān is certain to experience a revival.
Will it be under the Prince of Wú?
How I regret that I am too old to witness it!"
Jíjùn's Zhào Qiū said:
"The Mandate of Heaven rests with Yān.
Within fifteen years at most,
Qín will surely be possessed by Yān again."
Comprehensive Mirror
The Consort's Star loses its brightness
Fú Jiān appointed his younger brother Fú Róng as the Governor of Jìzhōu.
As Fú Róng was about to depart,
Fú Jiān bid him farewell east of Bà Bridge,
with music played and poems composed.
Fú Jiān's mother, Madame Gǒu, doted on Fú Róng as her youngest son.
She cherished him deeply.
By the time of his departure,
she had gone to Bà Bridge three times.
That evening, she secretly went to Fú Róng's residence again,
with no one inside or outside the court aware.
That night,
Fú Jiān was resting in the front hall
when the Grand Astrologer Wèi Yán reported:
"The Consort Star within the screen at the southern gate of the Celestial Market has dimmed,
and the attendants and eunuchs observe no sign of the consort's movement."
Fú Jiān investigated and learned the truth,
exclaiming in astonishment:
"How closely Heaven's way aligns with human affairs!"
Thereafter, he held astrological officials in high regard.
(From the "Records")
A baleful star appeared in the constellation Eastern Well.
In the final years of Fú Jiān's reign,
an ominous star appeared in the constellation Jǐng.
Yǐn Wěi, knowing that Jiān was about to be destroyed,
joined Yǐn Xiáng and Páng Yǎn in supporting Yáo Chàng as their alliance leader.
"Records of the States."
A yellow star appeared between Mǎo and Bì.
In the 21st year of the Tàiyuán era of Jìn,
a large yellow star appeared in the region between Mǎo and Bì for over fifty days.
Wáng Xiān, the Grand Historian of the Mùróng clan, said:
"A true leader shall rise between Yān and Dài,
his mighty army unstoppable, with weapons clanging."
In the winter, the eleventh month,
the yellow star appeared again,
and none under heaven could rival it.
This was the first year of the Huángshǐ era of Emperor Tàizǔ of Yuán Wèi.
From the "Wèi Shū"
Zhènxīng is in Xuānyuán.
Jǔqú Méngxùn heard that Liú Yù had destroyed Yáo Hóng,
and turning to his attendants, said:
"In ancient times, armies did not violate the position where Jupiter was stationed.
The Yáo clan
were descendants of Shùn and Xuānyuán.
Now Jupiter is in the Xuānyuán constellation, yet Yù destroyed them—
he too will not be able to hold Guānzhōng for long."
Later, Liú Yù's son Yìzhēn was indeed defeated by Hèlián Bóbó.
"Records of the States."
Mars strayed from its orbit
Initially,
in the year before Yáo Xīng's death,
the Grand Astrologer reported that Mars was within the Gourd constellation,
but one night it suddenly vanished without a trace.
Some said it had descended into a doomed state,
where it would manifest through children's rhymes and ominous rumors,
before unleashing its calamities.
Emperor Tàizōng was alarmed upon hearing this,
so he summoned eminent scholars,
ordering them to collaborate with the court historians to determine its whereabouts.
Cuī Hǎo responded:
"Allow me to deduce it by the celestial cycles.
On the evening of the gēngwǔ day,
and the morning of the xīnwèi day,
the sky was overcast—
Mars must have vanished within these two days.
Both gēng and wèi correlate with the state of Qín,
while xīn represents the western barbarians.
Now that Yáo Xīng holds Xiányáng, Mars has entered Qín."
The others mocked him for lacking evidence,
but Cuī Hǎo laughed without rebutting.
Over eighty days later,
Mars indeed emerged near the Well constellation,
lingering and circling there.
A severe drought struck the Qín region,
and the following year,
Yáo Xīng died.
Hostilities erupted within two years,
and by the third year, his state was annihilated.
Thereupon, the others conceded in admiration:
"This is beyond our grasp."
(Book of Wèi)
The troops await Tàibái.
When the deposed emperor perished,
Shěn Yōuzhī intended to raise an army.
He consulted his astrologer, Gé Kēzhī.
Kēzhī said:
Since ancient times, all who raise armies await the Great White Star (Venus),
when the Great White Star appears, they succeed;
when it hides, they fail.
In the past, Guìyáng launched his army when the Great White Star was hidden,
and was defeated in the first battle,
this is clear proof from recent times.
Now, Lord Xiāo has deposed the foolish and established the wise in governance,
coinciding with the time of the Great White Star's appearance,
this aligns with Heaven's will.
Moreover, the Great White Star will soon appear in the east,
the east favors the use of arms,
the west does not,
so Yōuzhī halted and did not rebel.
Later, when he raised his army,
Kēzhī again said:
This year, Jupiter stations in the Southern Dipper,
its state cannot be attacked.
Yōuzhī did not heed this,
and thus was defeated.
《Book of Sòng》
The courier star shoots across the sky.
Róngchéng Magistrate Xú Lù was skilled in divination by observing celestial phenomena.
During Emperor Shìzōng's reign, he was imprisoned in Jìzhōu due to an offense.
Assistant Inspector Cuī Lóngzōng visited him in confinement to offer consolation, and Lù said:
"Last night, the Courier Horse Star streaked across the sky,
predicting that a pardon should arrive imminently."
Lóngzōng initially believed him,
so he sent someone outside the city to wait and observe.
Shortly after, the pardon arrived.
Contemporaries held him in high regard.
"Book of the Later Wèi"
Cuì Yáng Tiāntíng
In the fourth year of Tàicháng of the Yuánwèi dynasty, from the first month to the autumn's seventh month,
the moon traveled westward trespassing against Tàiwēi,
the celestial phenomenon seeming to say:
"Tàiwēi is the pure Yang's heavenly court,
the moon is the minister,
yet now it crosses horizontally and treads upon it,
is this not exceedingly excessive?"
"Records of Celestial Phenomena"
Mars enters the Southern Dipper
In the sixth year of the Zhongdatong era of Emperor Wǔ of Liáng,
Mars had previously entered the Southern Dipper,
departed and then returned,
lingering for six days.
The emperor, citing a proverb that said:
"When Mars enters the Southern Dipper,
the Son of Heaven walks barefoot from his hall,"
removed his shoes and descended the hall to avert the omen.
Upon hearing that the Wèi ruler had fled west,
he remarked with shame:
"Could the northerners also respond to celestial signs?"
(Basic Annals)
Míng of Wèi asked Huáng Quán:
"With the empire divided into three powers,
which region holds legitimacy?"
He replied:
"We must examine the heavens."
Previously, when Mars guarded Heart and Emperor Wén died,
while Wú and Shǔ remained peaceful,
this was the portent."
(Records of Shǔ)
Mars enters the Well constellation
Chuán Yì,
during the Kāihuáng era of the Suí dynasty, served as an official in the Ministry of Rites under Hànwáng Liàng.
When Liàng raised troops in rebellion,
he said to Chuán Yì:
"Now Mars has entered the Well constellation,
what omen is this?"
Chuán Yì replied:
"The Well constellation in the sky,
lies along the path of the ecliptic,
which is precisely where Mars travels through,
this is not considered an anomaly.
If Mars were to enter a well on earth,
that would indeed be a disaster."
Liàng was displeased,
but after Liàng's defeat,
Chuán Yì was spared execution because of this.
From the Old Book of Táng.
The central star does not hold its position.
Wú Qiáo,
a native of Zháxī.
In the first year of Emperor Yáng's reign, while passing through Yèzhōng,
he informed the local magistrate:
"The central stars are not guarding Tàiwēi,
indicating suspicion towards the sovereign,
while the flourishing energy gathers in the land of Qín.
Are you aware of this?"
The magistrate did not believe him,
but only when Emperor Shénróng ascended the throne did he realize it was true.
Qiáo was proficient in astronomy,
and was the teacher of Yuán Tiāngāng.
"Records of Lóngchéng"
The golden jade bed sways
Emperor Yáng of Sui visited Jiāngdū,
and banditry grew daily.
Xiàhóu Duān was quite knowledgeable in celestial phenomena,
and skilled in physiognomy.
He advised Gāozǔ, saying:
"The golden jade bed shakes,
this signifies the emperor's throne is unstable.
The constellation Shēn is in its ascendant year,
so a true leader is bound to arise from the Shíchén sector.
The world is descending into chaos,
but the one who can bring order to it will be you, my lord."
The Virtuous Star guards the Qin region.
Xuē Shùn,
in the early Wǔdé era entered service directly in Prince Qín's residence,
and secretly stated:
"The virtue star guards Qín's territory,
the Prince shall possess the empire,
the Prince recommended him as Grand Historiographer's Assistant.
"Táng Shū"
Tàibái appears in Qín's territory.
Chuán Yì
secretly submitted a memorial in the fifth month of the ninth year of the Wǔdé era,
stating that Venus appeared in the Qin region,
indicating that the Prince of Qin would possess the empire.
Emperor Gāozǔ presented the memorial to Tàizōng.
When Tàizōng succeeded to the throne,
he summoned Chuán Yì, bestowed a meal upon him, and said:
"Your previous memorial nearly brought disaster upon me,
but from now on, you must speak out fully,
without worrying about past events."
"Old Book of Táng"
A comet appears in Tàiwēi.
During the Zhēnguàn era,
Tàizōng intended to perform the Fēng and Shàn ceremonies at Mount Tài,
when a comet appeared in the Tàiwēi constellation,
encroaching upon the throne's position.
Xuē Shùn stated:
Upon examining celestial phenomena,
it may not be appropriate to perform the Fēng ceremony in the east.
Chǔ Suìliáng said:
Just as we were to announce success at Dàizōng and a comet appears,
this indicates Heaven's will is not in accord,
I hope for more careful consideration.
An edict was issued to cancel the Fēng and Shàn ceremonies.
"History of the Táng Dynasty"
The Seven Stars Transform into Humans
During the reign of Tàizōng,
Lǐ Chúnfēng reported that the seven stars of the Big Dipper would transform into humans.
The next day,
they went to the West Market to drink wine, and he sent someone to observe them.
There were seven monks drinking two dàn of wine together.
Tàizōng dispatched someone to summon them,
but they laughed and said:
"That must be that youngster Lǐ Chúnfēng talking about us over there,"
and suddenly disappeared.
From "Zhōu Shǐ Zuǎn Yì"
Mars trespasses against the Five Feudal Lords
In the second year of the Cháng'ān era,
Mars encroached upon the Five Feudal Lords constellation.
Imperial Astronomer Shàng Xiànfǔ memorialized:
"My destiny's elemental sound lies in Metal,
and the Five Feudal Lords is the Grand Astrologer's position.
Mars is Fire,
which can overcome Metal.
This is an omen of my impending death."
Empress Wǔ Zétiān said:
"I shall perform a ritual to ward off misfortune for you."
She immediately transferred Xiànfǔ to the position of Commander of Waterways.
Stating:
"Water can generate Metal,
and now you are leaving the Grand Astrologer's position.
You need not worry anymore."
That autumn, Xiànfǔ died,
and Wǔ Zétiān sighed deeply in surprise and regret.
Old Book of Táng
Zhèn fàn Tiānguān
In the fourth year of the Cháng'ān era, Mars entered the moon,
and Saturn trespassed against the Heavenly Pass.
Yán Shànsī memorialized, saying:
"The celestial signs indicate that a disloyal minister will be punished for plotting against the sovereign."
A little over a year later,
Zhāng Jiǎnzhī, Jìng Huī, and others raised troops,
executed Zhāng Yìzhī, Zhāng Chāngzōng, and the five princes,
and established Zhōngzōng as emperor.
Old Book of Táng
The family below is drinking wine.
Zhāng Qiú Jiānqióng governed Western Chuān,
and once ordered a search for practitioners of the Daoist arts.
There was a wine seller who was not eager for profit;
four individuals wearing gauze hats and carrying calamus staffs would often come to drink several dǒu of wine,
and when the accumulated amount reached over ten shí, they would repay it all at once.
In their conversations, they frequently mentioned Sūn Sīmiǎo.
Someone reported this to Lord Zhāng Qiú,
who then specifically ordered an investigation.
Suddenly one day, they came again,
so the lord stealthily went to see them,
accompanied by three or four attendants.
When the lord approached them,
he leaped out, bowed twice, and announced his name.
They looked at each other and slowly rose, leaving only four pieces of burnt wood in front of the seats,
and were never seen again.
At that time, Emperor Xuánzōng favored Daoism,
so the lord reported the incident,
and an imperial decree summoned Sūn to inquire about it.
He said:
"These are the Taibái wine stars,
whose immortal rank is extremely high.
They often roam the human world to drink wine,
and can be found everywhere,
but they particularly enjoy Shǔzhōng."
From "Unofficial History of the Táng"
Sūn passed away in the first year of the Yǒngchún era,
so how could it be said that Sūn was summoned for questioning here?
Běidǒu Transforms into a Pig
Monk Yī Xíng once had a favor from Granny Wáng,
Granny Wáng's son committed murder and was imprisoned,
Granny sought help from Yī Xíng.
Yī Xíng then moved a large urn into the Húntiān Temple,
and gave cloth bags to two servants, saying:
In a certain district's abandoned garden, at dusk, seven creatures will come in,
you must capture all of them.
After yǒu hour, indeed a herd of pigs arrived,
the servants caught them all.
Yī Xíng ordered them placed in the urn.
Emperor Xuánzōng urgently summoned Yī Xíng,
asking:
The court astronomer reported that last night the Big Dipper was not visible,
what omen is this?
Can you, Master, perform an exorcism for it?
Yī Xíng said:
During the Later Wèi period, Mars was lost,
and now the Emperor's Chariot is not seen.
What has never occurred in ancient times,
Heaven is giving a great warning to Your Majesty.
It would be best to grant a general amnesty to the empire.
Xuánzōng complied.
Yī Xíng returned and released the pigs.
That same evening,
the court astronomer reported one star of the Big Dipper had appeared,
and within seven days it fully recovered.
"Yǒuyáng Zázǔ"
A star trespasses against the Pleiades.
Wéi Jiànsù met Emperor Sùzōng in Shùnhuà Commandery.
In the tenth month of that year, on the day Bǐngshēn,
a star trespassed against the Pleiades.
Wéi Jiànsù said to the Emperor:
"The Pleiades represent the Hú people.
Heaven's way shows portents whose responses are in humans—
Ān Lùshān is about to die."
The Emperor said:
"Can the exact month and day be known?"
Wéi Jiànsù replied:
"Blessings correspond to virtue,
disasters correspond to punishment.
The Pleiades, being metal, fear the fire phase.
When fire is in position and the Pleiades culminate at dusk, that will be the time.
He will die in that month and on that day.
Next year, on the jiǎyín day of the first month,
Ān Lùshān will perish!"
The Emperor asked:
"How will the rebel die?"
He answered:
"According to the theory of the five phases,
the son looks to what the wife gives birth to. The Pleiades' trespass on Bǐngshēn involves metal and wood—
the consort,
being the mother of wood and fire.
Bǐng fire is the son of metal,
Shēn is also metal.
Two metals are originally the same but ultimately different;
they return to overcome each other.
The rebel will likely be killed by his son,
and the chief instigator
will be slaughtered in turn."
When Ān Lùshān died,
the month and day were both verified.
New Book of Táng: According to the basic annals of the New and Old Books of Táng,
Ān Lùshān died on the yǐmǎo day,
so the statement "both verified" here is questionable.
Mars stations at Jupiter
When Zhū Cǐ usurped and occupied the capital,
and Lǐ Shèng stationed his troops at the Wei Bridge,
Mars remained near Jupiter for a long time.
Just as it retreated,
some aides and advisors urged him:
"Now that Mars has retreated,
it is advantageous for the imperial house.
We should quickly launch an attack."
Lǐ Shèng replied:
"The Son of Heaven is residing outside the palace,
and as subjects we should only be ready to die for our principles. The celestial phenomena are profound and distant,
how can I presume to understand the ways of Heaven?"
After recovering the capital, he told his staff:
"Previously when the officials urged me to send out troops,
I dared not refuse them outright.
An army can be commanded but should not be made aware of everything.
I have heard that the movements of the five planets are unpredictable.
I feared that Mars might return to Jupiter's position,
which would cause our army to collapse without even fighting."
His staff sighed in admiration,
and all said:
"This is beyond our comprehension."

Old Book of Táng
Tàibái violates the superior minister
In the eighth year of the Yuánhé era, the planet Venus trespassed upon the Shangxiang constellation and passed through the Zhifa constellation.

the court astronomer Lǐ Jǐngliàng reported that the literary star had dimmed,

Shěn Xún, serving as Vice Minister of Rites,
heard this and grew concerned.
By this time, all three examination categories underwent re-examination for the Hóngcí exam,

Vice Minister of Personnel Péi Shěn was demoted to Chancellor of the National University,

Hú Táo, being the son of an old acquaintance among colleagues,
attempted to shift blame for the leaked exam topic onto Táo,

The wood enters the Southern Dipper
During the Qiánfú era of the Táng dynasty,
the planet Jupiter entered the Southern Dipper,
and remained there for several nights without receding.
Wáng Duó, the military governor of Jīngzhōu, consulted astrologers,
who all said:
"When Venus, Mars, or Saturn offend the Dipper, it brings disaster,

Jupiter entering the Dipper

Picture of the God of Longevity
In the winter of the eighth year of the Jiāyòu era, in the eleventh month,
a Daoist roamed the capital's markets practicing divination,
with none knowing his origins.
His appearance and form were peculiarly strange, unlike ordinary people,
he drank immeasurable amounts of wine yet never appeared intoxicated.
The capital's residents found him extraordinary and spread word excitedly,
curious individuals secretly sketched his likeness,
later reaching the emperor through close attendants,
who summoned him for an audience,
bestowed upon him one dàn of wine,
of which he drank up to seven dǒu.
The next day, the Directorate of Astronomy reported the longevity star approaching the emperor's throne.
Suddenly
the Daoist vanished from his location.
Emperor Rénzōng marveled at this for a long time.
Reviewing the countless longevity star paintings in the world,
they merely depict bending over turtles and fondling cranes,
with pines and cypresses interspersed,
adorned brightly with colors and nothing more.
During Rénzōng's reign, the world was prosperous and all things flourished as in spring,
fitting that the longevity star would sport in the mortal realm,
personally appearing before the emperor.

The star governs Zhōngguó
Some say the division of celestial fields
is exclusively possessed by China.
The star stations do not touch the barbarous regions;
is it that the sun and moon shine with partiality?
Lǐ Chúnfēng said:
Huáxià is at the center of the four intersections, occupying the correct position of the two principles (heaven and earth),
while the four barbarians have biased qi, with extreme heat and cold,
speaking bird languages and having beastly hearts,
how can they be mentioned in the same breath?
Thus Confucius said:
the barbarians,
and so forth.
Their perishing refers to this.
Therefore, Yuècháng with repeated translations,
the Xiōngnú knocking their heads on the ground,
Sùshèn presenting arrows,
the Western Róng listening to pitch-pipes,
all without exception cross seas and scale mountains.
Distant lands bring tribute,
people and livestock bow their heads inward,
different kinds settle their hearts,
speaking from this, it is evidence that the four barbarians revere China.
Thus Confucius said:
governing with virtue,
and so forth.
Surrounding it, moreover, the sages observed the phenomena and allocated them to states and regions,
sometimes taking what is produced by water and soil,
sometimes looking at what is suitable according to the wind and qi,
thereby connecting them to form correspondences in images.
Thus the Pleiades represent the image of disheveled hair,
Qīngqiū the tattooed country of barbarians,
Gěnghé the custom of Hu riders carrying spears,
the Hu people serving heaven mainly through the Pleiades star,
the Yuè people observing and discerning omens through the Dipper and Ox,
the Qín people divining with Wolf and Bow, the Qí observing Xū and Wēi.
Each affirms its own state,
its own object of reverence,
thus the sages, based on the inclinations and nature they felt, divided and assigned them.
How could this be arbitrary and forced matching?

This differs from the theory of Southern Jambudvīpa.

the second to govern Chǔ,
the third to govern Liáng,
the fourth to govern Wú,
the fifth to govern Zhào,
the sixth to govern Yān,

The five stars of the Five Chariots, their
station is at Bì star; the "Book" considers the northwest star to govern Qín,

the central star to govern Chǔ,

Then, what the Northern Dipper and Five Chariots govern are also these twelve states.

the various states; Zhèng Jiājì
said
so

According to this, these three books all do not reach the level of "Yǐsì Zhàn",
Why is that?
Explanation of the Character "Sù"
The "Shìmíng" states:
A constellation,
is a lodging,
meaning the stars each come to rest in their proper place.
． The "Shuōyuàn Biànwù" chapter says:
The so-called twenty-eight constellations,
are where the sun, moon, and five planets lodge.
Wáng Chōng's "Lùnhéng" states:
The twenty-eight lodgings serve as the residences for the sun and moon,
just as the earth has postal stations serving as offices for officials.
The Jìn "Tiānwén Zhì" says:
They are distributed in the four directions, seven in each, making twenty-eight lodgings.
Considering these accounts,
it is clear that "sù" means to lodge or rest,
and should be read with its original pronunciation.
In the "Wǔdū Fù," the line "exhausting the perches of flying and running creatures,"
uses "sù" in rhyme, borrowing to mean piercing through the layered heavens for a lofty hunt—this is merely a rhyming adaptation,
and one should not rigidly insist on pronouncing "sù" as "xiù."
The "Shǐjì Lǜshū" commentary's correct meaning gives both "xiù" and "sù" as pronunciations.
Conduct and demeanor differ in name.
When stars reside, it is called a station,
called a lodge,
called a stay,
sharing the same lodge is called a conjunction,
transforming into ominous stars is called dispersion,
passing through is called traversing,
striking each other is called a conflict,
furthermore:
separating and reuniting,
reuniting and separating is called a conflict,
appearing early is called excess,
appearing late is called deficit,

Four Cardinal Directions and Four Intercardinal Directions
Wind is the chaotic energy of yin and yang, stirred and aroused by agitation.
It is like the inner energy in humans,
which bursts forth due to intense emotions like joy, anger, sorrow, or delight.
Thus, the spring energy is warm, and its wind is gentle and harmonious,
a wind of joy.
The summer energy is abundant, and its wind blazes with fury,
a wind of anger.
The autumn energy is vigorous, and its wind is clear and chilly,
a wind of clarity.
The winter energy is solid, and its wind is harsh and fierce,
a wind of steadfastness.
These are the four cardinal winds.
Additionally, there are the four diagonal winds:
the northeast wind, Míngshù,
where all things emerge from darkness into light;
the southeast wind, Róngfēng, whose path fosters growth;
the southwest wind, Qīngmíng, where all things reach full maturity;
and the northwest wind, Bùzhōu, a time for concealment and storage.
These eight winds vary in energy across regions,
differing in speed and intensity.
When harmonious, they bring smoothness;
when contrary, they bring calamity.
There is no external force driving them;
it is the natural accumulation of energy.
In anger, they whip up sand and stones,
uproot trees and tear off roofs;
in joy, they do not even stir branches or grass,
distributing energy in accordance with all things—this is the nature of heaven and earth,
the essence of spontaneity.
